title: Fields medalist Jacob Tsimerman announces move to OpenAI safety research
subtitle: The Toronto number theorist took the field's top prize at the ICM in Philadelphia and used the podium to say the mathematical career "will not exist in its current form" and that he is joining OpenAI's safety work.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Jacob Tsimerman, a University of Toronto number theorist, accepted the 2026 Fields Medal at the International Congress of Mathematicians in Philadelphia on July 23 for his proof of core cases of the André–Oort conjecture and his reshaping of o-minimality theory into a tool for arithmetic geometry. At the press conference following the ceremony, he announced he would join OpenAI's safety division in August. Greg Brockman, Sebastien Bubeck, and Boaz Barak welcomed the move publicly, framing it as a boost to OpenAI's mathematical-guarantees line of work on model behavior.

The reason he gave is the newsworthy part. Tsimerman told reporters he believes AI systems will soon surpass human mathematicians and could pose a severe threat, and that he is pivoting toward finding mathematical certainty for AI safety. "The mathematical career, as we know it, I don't think it will exist in its current form," he said. Coming from a fresh Fields medalist — the field's highest honor, awarded once every four years to at most four mathematicians under 40 — the statement lands harder than it would from a commentator.

The move fits a pattern. Terence Tao has spent the past year publicly experimenting with AI-assisted proof work; Timothy Gowers has argued that AI mathematical assistants are already changing how research problems are approached; and Anthropic and DeepMind have both recruited senior mathematicians onto interpretability and evaluation teams. The theoretical-math community, long insulated from industry, is being drawn in by both curiosity and concern about what the next generation of models will do to the profession's foundations.

For learners and students considering a research career, the takeaway is neither "math is over" nor "go work at an AI lab." It is that the safest mathematical bet right now is on the parts of the field that make claims about AI systems verifiable — formal verification, proof assistants, learning theory, interpretability. Those are exactly the tools a Fields medalist just moved to a lab to build.
